Numerical experiments indicate the proposed method can significantly accelerate the matrix filling process with no loss in accuracy.

articleTitle: Decoupled potential integral equation applied to complex geometries
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we present a numerical implementation of the Decoupled Potential Integral Equation DPIE. The DPIE formulation allows to describe the scattered electromagnetic field by solving a boundary value problem for the vector and scalar potentials A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">scat</sup> and ø<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">scat</sup> separately. The formulation allows to obtain the exact scattered electric and magnetic fields for any frequency ω ≥ 0. The formulation is immune to low frequency breakdown, high density mesh breakdown and internal resonances. The formulation can be applied to multiply connected geometries without loop search. In this paper we present a low frequency multilevel fast multipole implementation of the DPIE based on a flat triangular discretization with piecewise constant basis functions and collocation method.

articleTitle: Broadband VHF radiometry with a notch-filtered antenna exhibiting a large impedance mismatch
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: VHF radiometry is employed in radio astronomy, ionospheric riometry, and in the measurement of signals and noise in communications applications. Accurate techniques for broadband VHF radiometry are well-known, however these techniques assume well-matched broadband antennas and/or receivers having real-valued input impedance over the bandwidth of interest. In this paper we demonstrate through theory and measurement the efficacy of accurate VHF radiometry over a large fractional bandwidth using a thin (thus, narrowband) dipole connected to a receiver whose first stage consists of notch filters that contribute significant and variable reactance throughout the passband. This technique facilitates the use of small antennas combined with aggressive notch filtering, resulting in compact systems that may be used in high-interference environments.

articleTitle: Backscattering modulation using strongly coupled magnetic resonance (SCMR) antennas
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: SCMR is a promising technology for remote sensing applications that require increased levels of power. This paper aims to develop the vital communication link between the sensor and reader in a similar way to passive RFID tags. A backscattering modulator and demodulator were designed and implemented using an SCMR system. Measured results indicate that using backscattering modulation is effective. This technology negates the need for other methods of communication, which may consume more power than desired.

articleTitle: Design of a ultra wideband remote sensing system based on Sub-Harmonic mixer
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a 325GHz Sub-Harmonic mixer with 70GHz bandwidth is presented. It will be used for a ultra wideband remote sensing system. The mixer circuit included planar Schottky diode in a balanced configuration, the passive RF/LO and IF matching networks, filtering circuits, as well as transitions from waveguide to suspended micro-strip. Simulated results for the 325GHz mixer achieved DSB conversion loss of 6.4dB. The LO pumped power was 6dBm at 162.5GHz. The conversion loss was less than 8dB from 290GHz to 360GHz.

articleTitle: Wideband leaky-wave radiation from wire-medium loaded Fabry-Perot cavity antennas
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Open planar structures including wire-medium slabs with vertically aligned wires are studied by means of a transverse equivalent network representation of the relevant homogenized structure. Modal properties are thereby retrieved using a transverse-resonance technique, whilst far-field patterns generated by elementary sources are calculated via reciprocity. The application of wire-medium layers to suppress radiation due to TEM in a Fabry-Perot cavity antenna excited by a vertical electric dipole is demonstrated, thus obtaining wideband leaky-wave radiation from the TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> leaky mode in the form of a linearly polarized conical pattern with wide angular scan range.

articleTitle: Accurate electromagnetic analysis of transmission line structures with finite-thickness conductors
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Accurate electromagnetic (EM) analysis is performed for transmission line structures with finite-thickness conductors. Traditionally, the analysis ignores the thickness of conductors to simplify the model but such an ignorance may not be allowed in many applications. In this paper, a rigorous three-dimensional (3D) model without any geometric approximation is established and the method of moment (MoM) with the Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) basis function is applied to the analysis. To enhance the accuracy of solutions, a robust singularity treatment technique is adopted to evaluate singular matrix elements and good results have been seen from a demonstrated numerical example.

articleTitle: Rapid surface-wave analysis of corrugated rods using asymptotic corrugations boundary conditions
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present an analytical method of treating corrugated rods that provides extremely rapid but yet accurate surface-wave modal solutions. Based on the ACBC- the asymptotic corrugations boundary condition, the formulation is simple and elegant, providing not only the dispersion relationship between the frequency and wavenumber, but also the explicit functional forms of the fields. Dispersion results obtained by our proposed method are validated with an independent full-wave solver.

articleTitle: QCTO lens design for conformal phased array antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Quasi-conformal transformation optics (QCTO) provides a practical approach to design nonmagnetic broadband medium for electromagnetic devices, here we present a novel hybrid method of QCTO with array synthesis, and apply it to conformal phased array antenna (PAA) design which makes the complex conformal PAA can behave like a geometrically different array with wide scanning range when surrounded with QCTO lens. Taking conformal circular and triangular arrays as examples, numerical simulations are given to show how arbitrary non-uniform PAA based on QCTO can radiate and scan as a uniformly spaced linear PAA with low sidelobe, which make all of the advantages of linear array, such as simple array synthesis and beamforming, can be retained in an arbitrary array with complex geometry.

articleTitle: EM education for non-EE undergraduate students
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: At the Department of Medical System Engineering, Chiba University, we have Electromagnetics (EM) as one of the fundamental subjects for the undergraduate students. This paper describes some features and problems of EM education for non-EE students at the Department.

articleTitle: All-dielectric optical nanoantennas
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Control of light at the nanoscale is demanding for future successful on-chip integration. At the subwavelength scale, the conventional optical elements such as lenses become not functional, and they require conceptually new approach for a design of nanoscale photonic devices. Recently, a new field of optical nanoantennas emerged offering most promising solutions to this problem. Most optical nanoantennas consist of plasmonic nanoparticles due to their ability to capture and concentrate visible light at subwavelength dimensions. But the main drawback in the visible frequency range is their intrinsic losses which affect strongly the overall performance of plasmonic structures limiting their scalability and practical use.

articleTitle: Printable planar dielectric passive microwave components
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Printable planar dielectric passive microwave components are investigated in this paper. Micron-size-thick films are printed on low-loss microwave substrates and considered as nearly perfect magnetic walls to realize microwave components. The permittivity contrast between the substrate and film is kept high in order to minimize the leakage power and consequently the insertion loss. An approximate theoretical technique is used to analyze the structures. The theoretical results are confirmed by experimental results and the results from a simulation-based numerical method. The impact of dielectric loss of the film is much less than that of the substrate, allowing realization of highly efficient components using films with medium loss properties (e.g., ε" = 3). Several prototypes including waveguide and antennas are fabricated by screen-printing and characterized at different frequencies.

articleTitle: Characteristics Mode Analysis of a dipole antenna loaded with DNG material
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Characteristic Mode (CM) Analysis of a dipole antenna loaded with DNG material is presented. The eigenvalues and eigencurrents are calculated as function of DNG material parameter variations. It is observed that by properly adjusting the DNG material loading the CM resonances of a dipole antenna can be shifted lower in frequency allowing antenna size reduction.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of VHF vector sensor antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A very high frequency vector sensor antenna is designed and implemented. The antenna is used to estimate the angle of arrival in azimuth and elevation of an incident electromagnetic signal by measuring its electric and magnetic field Cartesian components. The Cramer-Rao lower bound is used for the analysis of the antenna's angle of arrival estimation performance. Furthermore, it is shown that the performance is highly affected by the presence of a conductive platform in close vicinity of the antenna.

articleTitle: Design and optimization of efficient wireless power transmission systems: Theoretical guidelines and experimental validation
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents the theoretical guidelines for the design and the optimization of wireless power systems (WPS) operating at different microwave bands. A set of representative experimental results concerned with different WPS systems operating in the S, X, and Ku bands are presented and discussed. The obtained results demonstrated the capabilities and the maturity of WPT systems as alternative power supply sources for supply low power electronic devices.

articleTitle: Slim UHF tag applicable to metallic film cans
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Hong Kong Film Archive stores more than 200,000 film reels. In order to facilitate the inventory and tracking of the film reels, a slim UHF metal tag is proposed. Though its antenna width is only 4.5 mm, it provides a read range about 3-5 m and is applicable to short metallic cylinder objects with diverse diameters.

articleTitle: Efficiency comparison between resonant coil and metamaterial sheet for wireless power transfer
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Resonant coils and metamaterials are useful to increase the effective range of a wireless power transfer system. We experimentally compared the characteristics of a resonant coil and a metamaterial with similar sizes. The resonant coil had higher Q and higher coupling ability with a loop than did the metamaterial. The transmission coefficient with the resonant coil system averaged 3.6 times higher than that with the metamaterial system.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable metasurface comprised of dogbone shaped conductor pairs
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A reconfigurable metasurface (MS) composed of a periodic array of dogbone shaped conductor pairs and embedded varactor diodes is analyzed with the aid of a qualitative analytical model and simulated numerically. It is demonstrated that electric and magnetic type resonances are independently controlled by applying bias to specific subsets of varactor diodes. The predictions of the analytical model are confirmed by full-wave numerical simulations and demonstrate tunability of the MS resonance response in a broad frequency range.

articleTitle: Improving the performance of null-field generation based preconditioner with approximate MLFMA technique
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we improve the performance of the efficient null-field generation based preconditioning scheme by combining with the approximate MLFMA technique. The impedance matrix generated by the null-field generation based scheme is more diagonal dominant than the conventional impedance matrix and fewer iterations will be achieved when far-field interactions are considered by AMLFMA technique. Representative numerical examples are given to illustrate the validity and efficiency of the proposed preconditioning scheme.

articleTitle: Low-permittivity EBG materials for antenna superstrates
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Suitability of low-permittivity EBGs to implement superstrates of high-gain resonator antennas is explored. Unit cell of the EBG is a square lattice with circular cross-section rods, with band-gap in the X-band. Permittivity of the rods is typical of PLA plastic filament used in 3D printing, with ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 2.76 and tan δ = 0.014. EBG cavity made by two identical mirrors separated by a resonating spacing is used to derive the antenna layout. The primary radiator is a rectangular patch, covered by the EBG mirror at a resonating distance, displaying a good gain enhancement. A further resonator antenna is devised, introducing a non-uniform spacing in the EBG rods along each layer of the superstrate. In this new layout, antenna gain and Side Lobe Level are considerably improved.

articleTitle: 60 GHz multi sin-corrugations Antipodal Fermi tapered slot antenna loaded with a spherical lens
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a hybrid antenna composed of spherical lens fed by an Antipodal Fermi tapered slot antenna (AFTSA). The AFTSA has customized multi-sin-shape corrugated patterns. The corrugation steps are used to enhance E and H- plane characteristics and reduce the return loss. The loaded methodology of the conventional semispherical is compared with new slotted full spherical lens. The model design achieved a gain of 20dB and 83% of total radiation efficiency at 60 GHz. Thus, the proposed antenna can be implemented in millimeter wave wireless communications and imaging detection systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of temperature rise generated by a titanium implant inside 1.5T MRI RF whole body coil
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We investigated transient temperature rise generated by a helix titanium alloy implant immerged into an ASTM phantom located inside 1.5T MRI RF whole body coil and 3D EM simulation simplification consequences. The location of the thermal hot spot and temperature rise were found to be dependent on implant electrical conductivity. In realistic simulation temperature rise at implant tip was noticeable less than maximum temperature rise around helix wire. After 15 minutes heating temperature rise in surrounding liquid was practically identical along entire implant structure.

articleTitle: Eigenmode expansion and mode-matching analysis of Bessel beam launchers
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: It was recently shown that a leaky radial waveguide can produce a propagating Bessel beam in free space. Two such waveguides can be coupled such that the fields are tightly confined in free space. Analysis of such a coupled system is presented here. Eigenmode expansion is applied to the leaky-waveguides, and mode-matching is performed. Computations show close agreement with simulation results of a commercial Finite Element Method (FEM) solver.

articleTitle: 60 GHz planar fresnel zone lens
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present the design guidelines of a planar Fresnel zone lens, where each zone has a certain permittivity. The different permittivities are realized by perforating a dielectric of higher permittivity. We designed a lens that adds 13 dB of gain to a patch antenna. A slightly modified fabricated sample shows a focusing gain of 10 dB in measurements.

articleTitle: EB scheme hybrid spectral-finite element time domain method for super multiscale simulations
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A hybrid discontinuous Galerkin spectral element and finite element time domain (DG-SE/FETD) method for the first-order Maxwell's equations is proposed in this study. It uses EB to replace the EH scheme in earlier research. The discontinuous Galerkin method is employed for domain decomposition. Non-conformal mesh allows not only an abrupt change of element size but also different element type across the interfaces between adjacent subdomains. Compared to EH scheme, the EB scheme has less DoFs, consequently, consumes less CPU time and memory. This new DG-SE/FETD method has been successfully applied to multiscale problems.

articleTitle: AIM-AWE technique for surface-wire integral equation
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The adaptive integral method (AIM) in conjunction with the asymptotic waveform evaluation (AWE) technique is utilized to deal with broadband electromagnetic problems of surface-wire junction geometries in this paper. The method of moments (MoM) is applied to the surface-wire integral equation (SWIE). And currents on conductor and wire surfaces are expanded by Padé approximant with respect to frequency to achieve fast frequency sweeping. The AIM is employed to reduce computation time and storage of higher-order derivatives of impedance matrices in the AWE. Numerical results show good efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Low SAR shorted dipole antenna for implantation applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A miniaturized dipole antenna is presented for implantation applications. The proposed antenna consists of two folded arms which are connected through a conductive plate. Whole antenna dimension is 7×9 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and suitable for ISM 2450MHz application. Both theoretical study and practical measurements indicate that the proposed antenna has low specific absorption rate and preserves the primary characteristics from tissue.

articleTitle: An impedance surface-based method for designing wideband reflectarrays
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a reflectarray antenna from the point of view of an impedance surface instead of the traditional array-based methods. The proposed design methodology is based on the Bessel filter with its group delay bandwidth maximized. It will be shown that the reflectarrays can fully capitalize this bandwidth without using true-time-delay devices. A proof-of-concept 1-D reflectarray is designed using the developed methodology. Simulated far-field patterns are shown and compared to a parabolic reflector.

articleTitle: A wide-angle scanning array based on the image theory and time reversal synthesis method
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wide-angle scanning array based on the image theory and time reversal synthesis method (TRSM) is proposed. The main lobe of the array can scan from -75° to +75° with a gain fluctuation less than 4dB. It shows that the image theory can be used to design wide-beam antenna and the TRSM can be used to optimize the wide-angle scanning array efficiently.

articleTitle: A system-by-design approach for the synthesis of metamaterial printed WAIMs
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a wide-angle impedance matching (WAIM) layer based on a metasurface structure is proposed to mitigate reflection issues for waveguide-fed planar phased arrays. To achieve this goal, the synthesis problem is formulated as a System-by-Design one where the degrees of freedom are represented by the geometry of the metasurface unit cells, and the objective is the minimization of antenna input reflections caused by impedance mismatching when the array is steered. The proposed solution technique is based on the combination of elementary functional blocks aimed at (i) exploring the search space, (ii) analyzing the resulting metasurface structure to deduce the equivalent permittivity/permeability tensors, (iii) computing the phased array response, and (iv) linking the obtained result with the problem constraints and objectives to determine the associated cost function. A preliminary numerical validation is illustrated to assess the effectiveness and flexibility of the proposed synthesis strategy.

articleTitle: A novel 3-D printed electrmagnetic bandgap structure for parallel plate mode suppression in microstrip circuit packages
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel 3-D printed electromagnetic bandgap structure is proposed for parallel plate mode suppression in microstrip circuit packages. The dispersion analysis of the proposed EBG shows that its stopband bandwidth is enhanced compared with the previous work and it electric size is reduced to 0.21λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.21λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.18λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. 3-D printing technique is used to print the prototype and a simple microstrip line is fabricated for testing its performance. The measured results show that the parallel plate modes in the stopband of the proposed EBG structure are suppressed and the insertion loss of the microstrip line is similar to that of the unpackaged one.

articleTitle: Comments on the size-dependence of focal point shift in offset-fed reflectarrays
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The impact of important factors such as aperture size (D) and focal length (F) on the amount of focal point shift in offset-fed reflectarrays is investigated using a full wave receive-mode analysis.

articleTitle: Equivalent circuit model of multilayer double square loop FSS using vector-fitting
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present the analysis and modeling of multilayer double square loop frequency selective surface adopting vector fitting procedure. The simulations of microstructure are performed with full wave simulation tool CST Microwave Studio on multilayer substrates with permittivity ranges from 2.2 - 4.3 in the frequency range 1 GHz - 30 GHz and substrate thickness ranges from 0.5 mm - 2 mm for different physical parameters. Then circuit models are extracted and developed using the vector fitting tool and implemented in a circuit simulator enabling both time and frequency analyses which includes the effect of polarization and angle of incidence. ADS SPICE generator is used for verifying circuit models developed using simulated results. The developed model is within 1% of average deviation against reference data.

articleTitle: Metaloop antenna with a parasitic loop
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An antenna composed of a fed metaloop and a parasitic metaloop is presented. The antenna characteristics for this double metaloop, including the radiation pattern, axial ratio, gain, and VSWR, are compared with those for a single metaloop where the parasitic metaloop is removed. The double metaloop antenna has a smaller cross-polarized radiation component than the single metaloop, leading to a wider axial ratio bandwidth of 20.6%.

articleTitle: Pancharatnam-Berry metasurfaces with giant nonlinear response
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We show that a generalization of the Pancharatnam-Berry phase approach can be applied to realize metasurfaces with giant nonlinear response, enabling a unique control of the generated nonlinear wavefront. We apply this approach to design and realize a nonlinear metasurface for efficient second-harmonic generation, which may independently tailor the radiated beam into right-handed and left-handed polarized components propagating with arbitrarily patterned wavefronts.

articleTitle: An oblique-angle infrared circular polarization filter using a Bezier surface representation
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a method to determine CO2 concentration by measuring relative circular polarization using 2D periodic unit cells of Bezier surfaces optimized using the Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy. The CO2 absorption spectrum has a peak which can be useful for measurement at 4.3 μm. A filter was designed to separate circularly polarized components of light at this frequency using the Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolutionary Strategy (CMA-ES). The filter presented is capable of blocking the effects due to nearby absorption bands such as the N2O band at 4.5 μm.

articleTitle: The propagating frame: A novel framework for wave tracking through rough medium and for inverse scattering
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a novel strategy for tracking wavefields in weakly fluctuating media. Using frame theory, we expand the aperture sources using a windowed Fourier transform frame, expressing the field as beams emerging from a discrete set of exit points and directions in the source domain. We show that, extending the frame concept into the propagation domain, the beams themselves constitute a frame, denoted the propagating frame. In this paper we show that the forward and backward propagating frames provide a full alternative to the conventional plane wave spectrum. We consider the simple problem of radiation from a volume source distribution and show that the beam expansion is obtained by projecting the source onto the propagators in the beam domain, an extension to the conventional plane-wave (Fourier) analysis. The propagating frame representation provides a new self-consistent framework for wave tracking through rough media, where the interaction of the propagating beams with the medium heterogeneities is analyzed locally, and then projected onto the same beam set. Applications for wave tracking through random medium and for inverse scattering will be presented.

articleTitle: Effect of chest wall on breast tumor detection using Prony's method
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Ultra wideband microwave imaging has been recently used as tool for breast cancer detection. The breast was represented as flat or semispherical or cylindrical model in previous researches. This paper studies the effect of including chest wall in breast model on tumor detection. Prony's method is applied on the scattered field from malignant breast to calculate complex natural resonance which are function of breast structure, tumor shape, and its electrical properties. Poles of malignant breast for two different chest wall models are compared with the one with no chest wall.

articleTitle: Parallel feed wearable ZigBee antenna with symmetry meander lines
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A flexile, compact textile antenna that operates in the 2.4 GHz Zigbee band is proposed. The substrate and conductive plane are constructed by textile materials, which make it is easily to be integrated with clothes and also comfortable to be wear. Two types of conductive materials are used to form the radiation element and ground plane. The measured result shows that the impedance bandwidth of antenna with SH is 5.1% and antenna with CFT is 1.62%. The minimum value of S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> of antenna with SH is -22.96 dB and antenna with CFT is -25.77 dB. The effects of human body and antenna bending are studied in this letter. The simulated and measured results show that the proposed antenna is very suitable for body area network.

articleTitle: Fast 3D nonlinear inversion method for airborne electromagnetic exploration
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an efficient three-dimensional nonlinear inversion method for airborne electromagnetic exploration. The stabilized biconjugate-gradient fast Fourier transform (BCGS-FFT) is used as the forward solver, and the distorted Born iterative method (DBIM) combined with the conjugate-gradient iterative solver is utilized in the inversion. Because of the usage of the FFT algorithm and the recursive matrix method combined with an interpolation technique to evaluate the layered media Greens functions rapidly, this method is highly efficient, and requires very low time and memory, O(NlogN) and O(N) respectively. Numerical examples for both 3D forward modeling and conductivity inversion are presented to show the accuracy and efficiency of the method.

articleTitle: Broadband fragmented cylindrical antennas
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new type of fragmented cylindrical antenna geometry is introduced that can be applied to common monopole and dipole antennas. Metallic regions of a cylindrical conductor are selectively removed in order to generate alternate current paths that can allow for increased operating bandwidth. Here, the metal patterning is optimized using the covariance matrix adaptation evolutionary strategy (CMA-ES) and a method-of-moments simulation tool to obtain antennas with a large operating bandwidth and quality radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Efficient analysis of EM scattering from 3D complex conducting objects buried under ground
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Electromagnetic scattering by three-dimensional complex perfect electrically conducting (PEC) objects buried under ground is investigated in this paper. The air-soil composite is approximated by a half-space model, where the half-space Green's function is adopted in the formulation of the electric field integral equation (EFIE). The simulation efficiency is improved from the following two aspects: a novel half-space Calderón preconditioner is developed to improve the spectrum of the EFIE operator, and thus the convergence rate of the matrix system; a half-space multilevel fast multitpole algorithm (MLFMA) based on real-image approximation is further adopted to accelerate each matrix-vector product and reduce the memory requirement. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of this method for the applications of underground detection.

articleTitle: Influence of body placement on low profile UWB antenna off-body ranging performance
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A study of human body influence on off-body ranging performance of a low profile UWB antenna is presented. Antenna ranging performance is reported for 10 volunteer wearers and for two different placements. Antenna was especially designed for WBAN applications and is immune to body influence even when in direct skin contact. Average ranging error value below 5 cm is observed for the majority of angles in the front antenna plane with standard deviation of the same order. The study shows that the antenna ranging precision depends more on the body placement than on the distance from the body.

articleTitle: Revisiting Levin+Li acceleration method for rapid diffraction analysis of reflector antennas
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Levin method, improved by Li, is shown to accelerate, by about three orders of magnitude, the brute-force physical optics radiation from a parabolic reflector of 240 wavelengths, especially in the far-out sidelobe regions. Key steps involve the use of an accelerating approximation involving a delaminating quadrature suggested by Li, sampling at Chebyshev-Lobatto nodes, the Chebyshev differential matrix, and truncated singular value decomposition. This paper revisits the application of the Levin+Li method and tailors it specifically to accelerate calculations for parabolic reflector antennas.

articleTitle: Source decomposition as a global absorbing boundary condition for multi-region problems
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A two dimensional implementation of the source decomposition method (SDM) is presented in comparison with the PML and Higdon absorbing boundary conditions for FDTD applications. The SDM is global in nature, however it can accommodate reflective external domains. The comparison shows that the results are of similar quality, indicating that the Higdon conditions can be a viable choice at a lower cost as far as nonreflective boundaries are concerned. The SDM is grid compatible and can be integrated into a general diakoptic scheme. It is expected to perform best over smooth boundaries, since corners tend to generate instabilities at the moment.

articleTitle: Circular array with dual conical beam pattern for emergency communications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a circular array working at 2 GHz capable of generating two conical beam patterns with a semiangle of 30° and 90° respectively. The genetic algorithm was employed in order to obtain the characteristics of the array. Four parameters were optimized by using this method: number of rings, ring radius, number of elements in each ring and phase excitations. As a result, three arrays formed by 1, 2 and 4 rings (12, 33 and 66 elements) were selected.

articleTitle: Design for suppressing undesired reflections from frequency-selective surfaces employed in multiband sector antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a technique that uses the small-metal width of a frequency-selective surface (FSS) element to suppress the change in beamwidth due to the undesired reflection from other FSSs. FSSs reflect low-level electromagnetic waves that are expected to pass through essentially the FSSs outside of the desired reflection bands, and generate these low level reflections from other FSSs as undesired reflections. Electromagnetic field analysis based on a dual-band antenna structure shows the relationship between the metal width and the reflection coefficient of the FSS element, and the relationship between the metal width and the beamwidth in the desired band and the other band. This paper clarifies that the small-metal width of the FSS element can be used to reduce the change in beamwidth outside the desired band.

articleTitle: Non-contact surface wave sensing of wire fault precursors
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A non-contact surface wave method of aging related insulation damage (fault precursors) detection in cables is proposed. Aging related hot spot detection is examined to demonstrate the efficacy of this method on an unshielded cable. A non-contact surface wave launcher launches a Gaussian chirp signal (120 MHz center frequency and 100 MHz bandwidth) onto the surface of a 22.9 ft. long power cable. The propagating wave is reflected from the location of the aging hot spot as well as from the open end. The time frequency cross-correlation clearly identifies the location of the aging hot spot.

articleTitle: Imaging effectiveness of multistatic radar for human body imaging
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Current state-of-the art active millimeter wave radar systems for personnel inspection are based on monostatic or quasi-monostatic configurations that can misrepresent areas of the target when the specular reflection is oriented away from the incident direction. This paper analyzes a fully multistatic mm-wave imaging architecture for human body screening. Transmitters placed off the receiving aperture panel maximize the surface of the human body that can be reconstructed. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated with 2D simulations. Three-dimensional simulation-based examples to validate the proposed system using realistic human body models will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: A broadband wide-angle polarizer through field transformation
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a broadband wide-angle polarizer based on a field transformation (FT) method. By adjusting the thickness of such a polarizer, we achieve polarization conversions between TE and TM, LCP and RCP, linear and circular polarizations respectively for both transmission and reflection cases. Such a polarizer can be realized through sub-wavelength dielectric gratings based on the effect media theory, their performance have been verified through full-wave numerical simulations and experiments in microwave regime.

articleTitle: Femtocell cooperation based on multiple-access channel model
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Femtocell access points (FAPs) has emerged as to improve the coverage and capacity of next generation network. However, dense femtocell deployments can cause severe interference. In this paper, a FAPs' cooperation approach is proposed to solve the interference problem. In particular, for uplink transmissions, the cooperative FAPs are allowed to form a group (i.e., coalition) to optimize their sum-rate by jointly decoding their received signals, and the FAPs' cooperation problem is formulated as a coalitional game in characteristic form with transferable utility based on multiple access channel (MAC). It is demonstrated that all the FAPs can form one group (i.e., grand coalition) to maximizes their sum-rate. Moreover, the core of the grand coalition is proved to be non-empty. Simulation results show that the proposed approach outperforms non-cooperative case in terms of the total system sum-rate and the average rate per link.

articleTitle: Implementation of an advanced tomographic algorithm for GPR realistic sounding
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Presented here is an advanced implementation of a microwave tomographic approach, which is capable of accounting for the near-field distribution generated by antennas commonly used in typical monostatic and bistatic Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) systems. The algorithm is applied to process numerical data obtained by means of a reliable and efficient full-wave simulation tool. This latter enables us to achieve an accurate determination of the electromagnetic field incident in the probed medium as well as of the backscattered field generated by metallic or dielectric hidden targets. Various non-ideal effects in the investigated scenarios are considered, in order to verify soundness and effectiveness of the reconstruction procedure.

articleTitle: Miniaturized multi-section crossover with open stub
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact branch line crossover using open stub structure is proposed. The proposed crossover operating at 2.5 GHz has a fractional bandwidth of 22 % (from 2.15 GHz to 2.72 GHz) with high isolation, high return loss, and low insertion loss. Size of the proposed crossover is reduced by 35-53 % comparing to previous papers.

articleTitle: Surface plasmon modes in self-biased coupled graphene-coated wires
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Plasmonic modes supported by a pair of self-biased coupled graphene-coated wires (GCW) are studied in detail. The proposed biasing structure enables the reconfiguration of the guided surface waves without additional gating electrodes, inducing a spatially variant conductivity that is calculated analytically. The eigenmode study of the structure reveals the presence of two fundamental modes with odd and even symmetry, which concentrate the fields in the gap between the wires and in the outer perimeter of the wires, respectively. The reconfigurable multimode behaviour and strong field enhancement induced by this structure may enable efficient light harvesting and nanofocusing in THz sensing systems.

articleTitle: Full-wave third harmonic generation analyses of graphene-based optoelectronic devices
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Over the past decades, a few prototype of graphene-based optoelectronic devices have been proposed because of graphene's remarkable optical and mechanical properties. However, few tools are available for analyzing graphene's nonlinear optical performance within practical designs, despite its strong third harmonic generation (THG) has drawn intensive attention in theoretical and experimental study. In this work, a full-wave solver is proposed for the THG problem. Based on boundary-integral spectral element solvers, the proposal numerical method shows relatively fast convergence and high accuracy. In addition, as a typical example, several prototypes of graphene-based photodetectors are studied for their THG emission as stored energy.

articleTitle: Wideband negative permeability structures based on split ring resonators
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, new wideband negative permeability structure is proposed. The structure consists of modified split ring resonator. The structure is developed by using FDTD simulations. The wide frequency range characteristics are confirmed by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: An Antenna for RFID tag printed on paper substrate using conductive ink
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, its presented the design of a dipole antenna with bent ends for UHF passive RFID tags printed on hydrophobic paper substrate. Silver particles conductive ink is used in an inkjet printer to build the radiating strips. This approach leads to significant benefits to users of RFID tags through low cost and fast fabrication and for being a green solution in large scale production. The energy to “wake up” the tag is obtained from the electromagnetic wave emitted by the reader which is captured by the tag antenna. Impedance matching is achieved through a careful design of the antenna to maximize the energy transfer and, as a consequence the reading range. The reading rate versus tag sensitivity is investigated. The tests were performed in a GTEM Cell which provides an electromagnetic radiation immune environment.

articleTitle: Compact broadband ZOR and FOR antenna with epsilon negative transmission line
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A zeroth-order resonance (ZOR) and first-order resonance (FOR) antenna based on the metamaterial is presented in this paper. The epsilon negative transmission line (ENG-TL) includes one meander line for realizing shunt inductance. The antenna is fed by an asymmetric co-planar waveguide (ACPW). The asymmetry of this structure brings about ZOR and FOR mode, which are merged into one passband to achieve a wideband performance. The ZOR and FOR antenna with high gain has a wide bandwidth of 1.60-3.34 GHz and a small size of 0.2λ×0.13λ.

articleTitle: A self-biased 3D tunable helical antenna in ferrite LTCC substrate
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A ferrite LTCC based helical antenna which also provides magneto-static bias for its frequency tuning is presented in this work. The 3D helical-cum-bias winding design avoids the use of large external electromagnets which are traditionally used with ferrite based tunable antennas. This reduces the overall size of the design while making it efficient by getting rid of demagnetization effect experienced at the air-to-ferrite interface. RF choke and DC blocking capacitor, required to isolate the RF and DC passing through a single structure, are integrated within the multi-layer Ferrite LTCC substrate. Magnetostatic and microwave simulations have been carried out for the design optimization. The prototype antenna demonstrates a tuning range of 10 % around 13 GHz. An optimized design with an air cavity is also presented which reduces the biasing power requirement by 40 %.

articleTitle: UWB printed monopole antenna with controllable multi notch function using rotational circular SRRs
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work proposes a new design technique to obtain multi notch function in an UWB response of a printed monopole antenna using rotational split ring resonators(SRRs). SRRs with rotated inner rings are inductively coupled to the CPW feed of the antenna. The relative angular variation of the SRR rings control the notch functions. The design is validated using an EM simulator. Experiments are underway and measured results will be presented.

articleTitle: On beamwidth effects on RCS of objects in random media for E-wave polarization
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper addresses effects of the beamwidth on the radar cross-section (RCS) of objects with different complexities in random media. We conider a random medium such as turbulence with various correlation functions. Horizontal incident wave polarization (E-wave incidence) is assumed.

articleTitle: Porcine skin as human body phanton at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This communication presents the results of an experimental campaign carried out at 60 GHz to demonstrate that porcine skin can be used at 60 GHz as a phantom for the human body. Norton formulations above a flat human body are verified using porcine skin.

articleTitle: Frequency selective transmission through waveguides with ENZ sections
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Multi-sectional waveguide structures providing frequency selective transmission controlled by transverse insertion of metal rods in the ENZ sections, are proposed and investigated by using full-wave simulations. It is demonstrated, that when the diameter of the inserted rod is adequately chosen, the position of the full transmission peak in the waveguide spectrum can be furnished at any frequency within the range of 0.75 GHz above the cut-off frequency of the ENZ section.

articleTitle: Suppressing higher order modes of cavity surrounded stacked microstrip antennas for prime focus reflectors
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A cavity surrounded stacked circular patch antenna is investigated as a feed for prime-focus reflectors in this paper. The radiation patterns of this feed are slightly asymmetric in the E-plane, which are improved by a differential feeding technique using two probes. This feed has a bandwidth of 20%, and wide beamwidths which improve the overall efficiency of symmetric parabolic reflector antennas.

articleTitle: Compact and multiband dielectric resonator antenna for mobile terminals
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact multiband internal dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) for mobile applications is presented, covering GSM/DCS/PCS/UMTS/LTE bands (880-960 and 1700-2700 MHz ). The antenna used a multi-branch monopole to stimulate a rectangular dielectric of high dielectric constant with a rectangular groove on its surface, thereby achieving not only reduced antenna size but also improved bandwidth. The overall size of the antenna is only 0 0.075λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0 0.045λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0 0.012λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> at 900MHz. This communication covers the details of the antenna design and simulation.

articleTitle: Design of multi-band uniplanar MIMO antenna for mobile devices with LTE/WLAN operation
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A multi-band uniplanar MIMO antenna for mobile devices, covering Long Term Evolution (LTE) and Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) bands is proposed. The antenna features two radiating elements composed of direct-fed and couple-fed monopoles with parasitic structures to allow wideband coverage. The MIMO design features four main operating bands, 695-963, 1790-2650, 3520-3702, and 5565-6348 MHz. The dimensions of the proposed MIMO antenna are 115mm × 55mm × 0.8mm with simple geometries that can easily be integrated into 4G LTE mobile devices.

articleTitle: Analytical and numerical modeling of passive and active coated nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A variety of open and closed nanoparticle structures have been considered analytically and numerically. These include multi-layered structures based on dielectrics and metals excited by plane waves and electric Hertzian dipoles at optical frequencies. Both passive and active (gain impregnated dielectric) materials have been considered. Enhanced and mitigated scattering effects have been modeled. Nano-antenna and nano-amplifier configurations for optical applications have been emphasized. A review of these modeling efforts will be presented.

articleTitle: Characterization of an on-body quasi-static channel in underground mine environment
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the on-body performance of three quasi-static channels was evaluated, when the human body undergoes certain typical movements. The main contribution of this work is the analysis of the impact of body movements on the performance of the on-body system in a mine environment. The quasi-static channels parameters were determined and compared to those of a corresponding static channel.

articleTitle: A new formulation discontinuous Galerkin Surface Integral Equation method for time-harmonic wave scattering problem
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new formulation Discontinuous Galerkin Surface Integral Equation (IEDG) method, which allows non-conformal mesh and square-integrable, L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, trial and test functions during simulations. Most of the important, it gives a more accurate solution of electric/magnetic currents distributted on PEC-dielectric boundary. This is very benificial in solving periodic PEC-dielectric structure, such as large-scale FSS radomes. In the end, Numerical calculations are carried out to validate the accuracy of this method.

articleTitle: A new family of radial angular transformations for the near-singularity cancellation technique
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new family of radial-angular-R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> transformation formulas are proposed for the singularity cancellation technique. To cancel out the singularity in the integral kernels, an ideal Jacobian of the coordinate transformations is required. For the first order of singular coupling integral kernels, a new augmented radial-angular-R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> transformation is proposed. For the second order of singular coupling integral kernels, new radial-angular-R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and radial-angular-R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-cosh transformations are developed. Finally, for the third order of singular coupling integral kernels, a new group of radial-angular-R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, arcsinh-R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and augmented radial-angular-R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> transformations are designed. The higher order singularity cancellation schemes are also effective for the lower orders of singular kernels. The proposed R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> transformation schemes are efficient and applicable to all mutual couplings for in electromagnetics integral equations.

articleTitle: Transmision line based approach for the synthesis of pattern reconfigurable antennas
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A design approach based on transmission line theory for the synthesis of pattern reconfigurable antennas is presented. It allows the design of a single input port parasitic elements antenna fulfilling user-defined requirements on a target radiation pattern. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated in dealing with a low profile directive antenna capable of switching its radiation pattern towards two opposite directions.

articleTitle: Using a contraction mapping method to determine complex permittivity from electromagnetic propagation measurements
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In typical logging while drilling propagation-resistivity tools, formation properties are measured at different operating frequencies. The conductivity and permittivity of the formation are obtained from the inversion of the measured amplitude attenuation and phase shift between a pair of receiver antennas. This paper describes a simple method for computing formation resistivity and permittivity from electromagnetic propagation measurements. It starts with a closed-form solution for a generic propagation tool in homogeneous and isotropic media and uses a contraction mapping method for inverting conductivity and permittivity.

articleTitle: Transient analysis of plasmonic nanostructures using an MOT-PMCHWT solver
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A marching on in time (MOT) scheme for solving the Poggio-Miller-Chan-Harrington-Wu-Tsai (PMCHWT) surface integral equation on plasmonic nanostructures is described. The proposed scheme calls for temporal convolutions of the permittivity and Green function of the plasmonic medium with the temporal basis function. Time domain samples of the permittivity and the Green function required by these convolutions are computed using a fast relaxed vector fitting (FRVF) algorithm. Numerical results demonstrate the accuracy and applicability of the proposed MOT-PMCHWT solver.

articleTitle: Mantle cloaking: Antenna applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, we discuss some of our latest results about the use of mantle cloaking in different antenna scenarios. Due to the intrinsic characteristics of the scattering cancellation technique, and, in particular, the needed interaction between the external field and the object to hide, mantle cloaking approach can be profitably applied in both receiving and transmitting antenna configurations. In particular, we will show that by exploiting cloaking technologies it is possible to conceive new receiving sensors exhibiting an optimized balance between the scattered and the absorbed power, as well as invisible transmitting antennas that can be placed in close proximity to other radiators without affecting their electrical and radiative performances.

articleTitle: Constructing nonstandard and high order FDTD schemes in cylindrical coordinates using spectral domain and modified equation methodologies
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Cylindrical FDTD schemes are useful for avoiding “staircasing” approximations found in Cartesian modeling. Conventionally, schemes of this type are of (2; 2) order of accuracy. A recently introduced spectral methodology, combined with the modified equation approach, is applied for the analysis of existing cylindrical schemes as well as for the synthesis of new nonstandard and high order ones.

articleTitle: LOCOMO satcom terminal: A switchable RHCP/LHCP Array Antenna for on-the-move applications in Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes the main features of a multilayer antenna panel for a low cost Ka-band Array Antenna for on-the-move applications. The LOCOMO satcom terminal is based on a dual-polarized low-profile antenna with trasmit/receive and RHCP/LHCP switching capability.

articleTitle: Empirical and theoretical characterization of Multioctave Planar Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Theoretical and empirical characterizations of Multioctave Planar Phased Arrays (MPPA) are highly difficult, complex and costly; rooted in MPPA's complexity and its huge data and metrics that encompass large spatial and frequency domains. This paper presents theoretical and empirical characterizations as applied to an MPPA called Traveling-Wave Antenna Array (TWAA). The physical model has 16×16 elements, fed with True-Time Delay (TTD) corporate feeds for wide-angle scan up to 60° off broadside over 2-12 GHz. Excellent agreements between theoretical and empirical data were observed except for angles beyond 45°. Merits and limitations of classical and numerical analysis approaches are discussed.

articleTitle: A design of SPDT switch using graphene device
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A graphene-based single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switch is presented for mm-wave applications. The proposed SPDT switch is realized by mounting graphene layers on the slot of slotted substrate integrated waveguide (SSIW). Simulations show the designed switch achieves a frequency bandwidth from 59.5 GHz to 60.8 GHz with -3 dB insertion loss. A minimum insertion loss of -1.1 dB is obtained at 60 GHz, the corresponding return loss and isolation are -36.1 dB and -34.5 dB.

articleTitle: Compact ACS-fed antenna for UWB applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel compact printed antenna using asymmetric coplanar strip (ACS) feed is proposed for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications. With the ACS-fed structure and the opening in the radiating patch, the antenna is miniaturized to a size as small as 15 × 19 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 3.1 to 11.35 GHz and stable H-plane omnidirectional radiation patterns. The simple uniplanar structure makes the proposed antenna easy for implementation. Details of the antenna design and simulation results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: V-band integrated on-chip antenna implemented with a partially reflective surface in standard 0.13-µm BiCMOS technology
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a V-band on-chip triangular planar monopole antenna using IBM 0.13-µm BiCMOS technology. A partially reflective surface (PRS), which is realized with a dual-layered Gangbuster type-4 FSS structure, is exploited to increase the antenna frequency bandwidth, radiation efficiency and gain. The overall size of the antenna, including the PRS, is 0.86 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The measured S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> is smaller than −17 dB from 54 to 66 GHz, while the maximum measured antenna gain is 1.42 dB at 69.5 GHz. The maximum simulated antenna efficiency is 41% at 65 GHz.

articleTitle: Mutual-coupling suppression for 60 GHz MIMO antenna using metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a unique approach to reduce the mutual coupling between two dielectric resonator antennas working at 60 GHz. To implement that, an array of metamaterial inclusion is employed between the two antennas. Proposed unit-cell is comprised of a modified shape of CSRR structure which has a large stop-band in the frequency range of 57-64 GHz. Applying array of metamaterials between DRAs can provide isolation of -45 dB at 60 GHz.

articleTitle: Characterization of a perfect absorber
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A perfect absorber (PA) is seen as equivalent to an ideal antenna (IA), except that it absorbs the power from any angle of incidence. Similarly to the IA, the absorbed power is maximal for all substances supported by the same physical structure. When defining the PA in this way, care should be taken to avoid the superdirective zone. This is done by using the constraint Q = 1 for the quality factor around the absorber. Possible applications for numerical simulations are outlined.

articleTitle: A polarization-controlled MIMO antenna with an optimum phase shift in accordance with various use scenarios
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a polarization-controlled MIMO antenna to realize ultra high-speed and high-capacity mobile communications. The proposed antenna is comprised of three orthogonal dipoles, which can be controlled using a weight function created based on the variation of cross polarization power ratio (XPR) and the antenna inclination angle. By adjusting a phase shift between the antenna elements to an optimum value in accordance with various use scenarios and XPRs, the MIMO channel capacity is increased significantly in comparison with a conventional fixed-phase shift antenna.

articleTitle: Diffraction and pattern perturbation effects in offset Gregorian reflector antennas with wideband feeds
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The offset Gregorian reflector system of the Square Kilometer Array radio telescope is required to operate with wideband feed (WBF) antennas down to very low frequencies, where reflectors become (electrically) relatively small. The considered WBF technologies are the log-periodic (Eleven) antenna and the quadruple-ridged flared horn. This paper investigates some of the performance degradation effects that are specific for the low frequencies and typical for these WBFs, including the feed pattern perturbations and diffraction. Several performance metrics, such as the antenna receiving sensitivity and side lobe levels are considered.

articleTitle: Multi-resonant AgNW/PDMS patch antenna for biaxial strain sensing
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A silver nanowire (AgNW) conductor embedded in a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) elastomeric substrate forms a microstrip patch antenna that can sense an applied biaxial strain. The flexible conductor and substrate allow the antenna to be repeatedly deformed by applied force. The two resonant modes of the antenna respond differently to strain applied in orthogonal directions and can be used to uniquely identify the biaxial strain state. The trends expected from the cavity model enable mapping of the change in the resonant frequencies to an applied strain state. Measured S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> data under biaxial strain verify the simulations.

articleTitle: An application of Heisenberg's Uncertainty principle to line source radiation
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Heisenberg Uncertainty principle is discussed and applied to the problem of line source radiation. As shown herein, the principle states that equation, where equation is the variance of the power pattern, equation is the variance of the square of the current distribution, I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is the power content of the current distribution and L is the length of the radiator Furthermore, the principle can also be used to determine bounds on the radiated power, directivity and radiation resistance for an arbitrary current distribution with full account of the element factor.

articleTitle: Design of low-cost uniplanar AMC structures for UHF applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work a low-cost uniplanar electromagnetic bandgap structure is presented, for antennas and microwave circuits working in the UHF frequency band. The proposed configuration is fully planar, easy to fabricate, designed on a PET substrate using a conductive ink, and based solely on metallic surfaces on layer interfaces, without the use of vias or other kinds of vertical connections.

articleTitle: A modification of the two-antenna method to determine the phase center location as well as the gain of a wideband antenna
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A technique is presented for determining the amplitude center or phase center location of a wideband Vivaldi antenna at measurement distances of a few wavelengths. It is based on the well known two-antenna gain measurement technique but makes the antenna separation a variable. The phase center separation is shown to be proportional to the derivative of a transmission matrix loss parameter which is constant and independent of the antenna separation. A linear least squares fit to transmission loss parameters measured at several antenna separations is shown to yield the antenna gain and phase center location.

articleTitle: Wideband circular polarized cross bow tie antenna with balun integration for X band communication
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Wide band cross bow tie (CBT) antenna with circular polarization (CP) and good gain operating at X band has been presented for satellite communication. Impedance transition from imbalanced 50 ohms to balanced 100 ohms is carried out by using exponential tapered microstrip line. Geometry modification of CBT for getting CP property is proposed in this work. Proposed compact, circular polarized cross bow tie antenna showed constant impedance with S11 lower than -10dB throughout X band with broadside gain of 3db. 3dB axial ratio bandwidth is found to be 12 %.

articleTitle: Miniaturized antenna for LTE wireless USB dongle applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact dongle antenna achieving the band of LTE 700 for fourth-generation (4G) technology is proposed and studied. A meandered monopole is using the spaces on the front side and back side of the substrate to compact the size. This antenna is printed on 0.8 mm FR4 substrate with an overall size of 60 × 12 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The antenna consists of a compact antenna portion of 20 × 12 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a small system ground of 40 × 12 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Using different widths of the monopole and proper controlling the coupling between the monopole and the system ground, a small monopole antenna for LTE 700 can be obtained. The strips of the monopole on the front and those on the back of the substrate are connected by two via-holes. From the measured results, the bandwidth of the antenna fits the required bandwidth of LTE 700. The antenna with a very compact size and good performances is suitable for USB dongle devices of LTE 700 system.

articleTitle: Planar, high-gain, substrate-integrated cavity antenna in the terahertz frequency range
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a planar and highly directive cavity type of antenna in the terahertz frequency range. The antenna consists of a frequency selective surface (FSS) and an open-ended narrow slotline dipole, which are both lithographically patterned on a high-permittivity gallium-arsenide substrate. The FSS in conjunction with the ground plane of the slitline forms a Fabry-Perot resonator and results in significant directivity enhancement. The simulation results show that the substrate volume determines the effective permittivity of the cavity for the resonance operation. The optimized antenna, which has a size of about 3600 μm × 3600 μm × 175 μm, produced a maximum gain of 14.6 dBi, a radiation efficiency of 55%, and side lobe levels of -14.0 dB and -16.4 dB in the two principal planes at a resonance frequency of 317 GHz.

articleTitle: 2×2 MIMO downlink OTA measurement based on CTIA guidelines
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Wireless industry through 3G Partnership Project (3GPP), and CTIA The Wireless Association has been studying, validating, and standardizing the 2×2 MIMO Downlink OTA tests since 2009. Especially, CTIA has already provided the guidelines for the MIMO OTA tests in both the Spatial Multiplexing, and Transmit Diversity scenarios. After highlighting some background of the well-documented Spatial Fading Emulation Technique in which an array of eight dual polarized antennas and a fading Emulator is used, the paper is presenting the MIMO OTA results of a testing campaign. The Absolute Throughput is the Figure of Merit for MIMO OTA and it has been measured versus both the power and the SIR (Signal to Interference Ratio) at the DUT (device under test) location. It has also been reported in a way that a visual representation of the DUT behavior as a function of the azimuth rotation is given.

articleTitle: Investigation of reduced height dual-polarized Archimedean spiral antennas with unidirectional radiation patterns
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact dual-polarized Archimedean spiral antenna is further investigated in terms of its axial dimension. The spiral antenna is center-fed and capable of generating two orthogonal circularly polarized waves over a shared frequency bandwidth. Parametric studies are performed to examine the impact of the antenna heights on the frequency responses of the dual-polarized Archimedean spiral antennas.

articleTitle: Short time state space method for human motion identification
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, UWB radar system is introduced and the applicability of the short time state space method (STSSM) is investigated for the extraction of micro-Doppler (m-D) features from a walking subject. A full wave model of human motion and the Boulic model are used to validate the proposed STSSM and calibrate the parameters before it was applied to experimental data. It is experimentally demonstrated that STSSM can successfully distinguish the motion of different body joints by identifying corresponding m-D frequencies.

articleTitle: Time-domain nonlinear finite element analysis of air breakdown using a simplified plasma model
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the time-domain finite element method (TDFEM) is employed to analyze the high power breakdown in air. During the breakdown process, the motion of free electrons generates plasma currents, which produce secondary fields that couple back into the externally applied fields and interact with the free electrons. Such a breakdown process can be described by a coupled electromagnetic-plasma system, where the electromagnetic fields are governed by Maxwell's equations and the plasma current is modeled by a simplified plasma fluid equation. Due to the nonlinear characteristics of the breakdown phenomenon, the coupled system results in a nonlinear second-order partial differential equation that is solved by TDFEM together with the Newton-Raphson method.
